Breath-cloud bred, a dusk Heavy with the stillness before snow Awaits its final precipitate; A distant, traffic-muffled "Late!" Is shuffling slowly closer. recent_candidates.title: Somewhere in the Woods of Alta, California
recent_candidates.excerpt: A wild-feeling place might just offer rest to a wild-feeling heart. < < < Emma Fulenwider / November 7, 2026 My hometown is like the letter “A” on a typewriter—most people can find it without looking but couldn’t point to it blindfolded. When I went away to college, I told people I was from Sacramento because that was the closest large city. If they asked what part of Sacramento, I’d say, “Up 80, towards Tahoe,” because Californians know where Lake Tahoe is. If they happened to be especially acquainted with the area, I’d say, “Above Colfax,” because locals tend to know where Colfax is. But NO ONE knows where Alta is. I’m from Alta, California. recent_candidates.title: Nvidia’s $4.5 trillion test of founder immunity
recent_candidates.author: Andrew Edgecliffe-Johnson
recent_candidates.excerpt: There’s little precedent in US corporate history for the crisis facing Nvidia after reports that Jensen Huang was targeted by a Chinese “honeytrap” operation . The national security implications of the allegation, the chipmaker’s founder-CEO’s centrality to his company’s growth story, and Nvidia’s pivotal place in the AI ecosystem all mean the fallout is likely to stretch further than other cases of executive infidelity. Nvidia’s board on Sunday announced an independent investigation, but expressed confidence in Huang. In his own statement admitting that he had been unfaithful to his wife, Huang said he remained “fully committed” to the company. Nvidia is, at the time of writing, the world’s second-most valuable company after Apple, with a market capitalization of $4.5 trillion — almost 12% of the Nasdaq 100 index. And no public company has been more important to the AI revolution or its impact on stock markets: The ravenous appetite from hyperscalers such as Amazon and Google for Nvidia’s chips propelled its annual revenue from under $11 billion to more than $130 billion between 2020 and 2025. The most bullish analysts think its sales will hit $1 trillion in 2029. Huang’s personal indiscretions do not change Nvidia’s order book. But he has been inseparable from its commercial success story, helming its new product presentations, negotiating the loans to customers that have made Nvidia “the central bank of AI,” and dealing directly with President Donald Trump and Chinese lead

recent_candidates.title: Anti-Waymo campaign relied on op-eds written with AI
recent_candidates.author: Max Tani
recent_candidates.excerpt: The News Opponents of AI-powered cars have been using artificial intelligence to get their message out in the news media. They’ve been waging a kitchen sink campaign, placing op-eds in local news outlets arguing the autonomous taxi company Waymo could cost jobs, endanger riders, deprive the government of information, and block fire trucks. The AI detection service Pangram found that many of the pieces were written with a significant amount of AI input, but none contain labels disclosing AI use. Several op-eds were drafted by a PR firm, said Ira Goldstein, the former head of New York’s Black Car Fund and the author of an op-ed in the New York Daily News. “A first draft of this OpEd was prepared by our PR firm at the time, which is standard procedure when working with a PR firm. I reviewed the OpEd, and made some edits. The PR firm then handled placement in the Daily News,” Goldstein told Semafor in a statement. “With all that said, I stand by every word in this OpEd and believe that AI being used without my knowledge, to write a first draft of a 700-word opinion piece pales in comparison to the economic and public safety damage that thousands of AI powered robotaxis will inflict on New York City.” (In the same statement, Goldstein said the PR firm in question later last year also dropped the campaign to work for … Waymo.) recent_candidates.title: ‘Put the posters in charge’: Inside the Democrats’ secret strategy to flood the internet with clips
recent_candidates.author: Max Tani
recent_candidates.excerpt: The News By January 2025, Paulina Mangubat knew the Democratic National Committee needed to change its digital communications approach dramatically. The organization had been shattered by a second loss to Donald Trump, in which the party had been strategically outmaneuvered by a new alternative media ecosystem that had helped Republicans circumvent traditional gatekeepers. The DNC didn’t have an online creator strategy beyond one Signal group chat with about 20 left-leaning creators, where it occasionally shared messaging. Its brand had never quite recovered from the 2016 campaign, when it was thought to have tipped the scales against then-presidential candidate Bernie Sanders. Voters saw the national party as overly invested in outreach tactics of the past, as exemplified by a widely-mocked February 2025 post in which its official X account shared a long, hard-to-read list of Democratic accomplishments. That spring, staff met at a weeklong offsite to regroup, and Mangubat, the head of content and creative, opened with a presentation of comments the DNC was getting on social media. “Our team took a lot of the online criticism to heart,” she recalled Friday. The committee decided to make a few key changes. Most visibly, it took a more combative and at times personal tone, an approach mirroring the national mood of Democratic voters. recent_candidates.title: Paraguay's bank collapse hits millions
recent_candidates.author: Brendan Ruberry
recent_candidates.excerpt: Paraguay’s president was removed from office and detained after the country’s largest digital bank melted down, leaving half the populace without access to funds and plunging the country into a political crisis. A youth-friendly banking app, Ueno collapsed amid allegations of insider lending and proximity to the country’s longtime ruling party, which is closely aligned with Washington. The app was credited with expanding access in a region where as many as one in four adults does not have a bank account ; its implosion was a “ kind of tsunami in the end ,” a political scientist said, and puts at stake “the credibility of a country that has spent years trying to establish itself as a stable , reliable destination for international investment,” a regional analyst wrote in Americas Quarterly. — Brendan Ruberry

recent_candidates.title: Eisenkot gets nod to form Israeli government
recent_candidates.author: Brendan Ruberry
recent_candidates.excerpt: Israel’s president tapped Gadi Eisenkot to try to form the country’s next government, kicking off a tortuous negotiating process that could oust long-serving Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu. While Eisenkot and Netanyahu differ in style and substance , both men reflect the “ monolithically anti-Palestinian stance that dominates Israeli politics,” an International Crisis Group expert told Le Monde. There is also little “real difference” between the two on Iran, an Israeli analyst said, though recent elections in the US and Israel have created further uncertainty around the simmering conflict: President Donald Trump said on Sunday that further US strikes were “ highly unlikely ,” while Iran — which has taken credit for Republicans’ poor midterm showing — said negotiations were paused following the “shock” election result. — Brendan Ruberry

recent_candidates.title: New York City congestion pricing hailed as traffic, pollution drop
recent_candidates.author: Jeronimo Gonzalez
recent_candidates.excerpt: New York City’s congestion pricing system appears to be working as vehicle traffic and pollution drop, and some believe higher tolls could bring yet more progress. Though the plan’s 2025 rollout was controversial — the US transportation secretary called it “ a slap in the face to working-class Americans ” — evidence suggests it is achieving its aims, with some analysts calling for authorities to go further by raising tolls, which have brought in $1 billion, sooner than scheduled. Similar plans in London and Singapore have led to improvements, bringing down the volume of traffic while increasing air quality. “One lesson [from New York City] is pretty clear: If you want less congestion, you need to make the congestion-causers pay ,” a Bloomberg columnist wrote. — Jeronimo Gonzalez

recent_candidates.title: Houthis strike Aramco tower in Riyadh
recent_candidates.author: Kate McKenna
recent_candidates.excerpt: Houthi fighters took aim at the financial district of Saudi Arabia’s capital on Sunday — one of the highest-profile areas to be targeted in the war. A drone-and-missile attack damaged the iconic Saudi Aramco tower , located in an area that, as home to international companies and luxury housing, is a symbol of the kingdom’s modernization. Near-daily attacks in Riyadh have upended life and also forced the cancellation of a high-profile economic conference, putting pressure on Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman as he tries to keep on track a multi-trillion-dollar effort to position the kingdom as a destination for global capital. Saudi Arabia faces “ only bad options as it tries to find a way out of the conflict,” The Wall Street Journal wrote. — Kate McKenna

recent_candidates.title: How Hinojosa’s win in Texas could bite Beshear
recent_candidates.author: By Ali Bianco
recent_candidates.excerpt: AUSTIN, Texas — Gina Hinojosa’s stunning victory put Texas at the epicenter of a political earthquake — and the aftershocks could upend Andy Beshear’s path to the White House. For months, increasingly frustrated Hinojosa allies publicly and privately pressured the Democratic Governors Association, which Beshear chairs, to help push her over the finish line, as many national Democrats and donors stayed on the sidelines. On Tuesday, Hinojosa dominated the race for the Texas governor’s mansion, riding a blue wave that swept Democrats into power across the country, including flipping six governorships in states won by President Donald Trump. Latino operatives who spoke with POLITICO feel vindicated — and are turning their knives on Beshear ahead of a potential 2028 presidential bid. “His presidential campaign is over,” said Sergio Gonzalez, a Democratic operative working on programs to turn out Latino voters in the midterms. Beshear “doesn't understand politics in the way that a president needs to understand politics,” and “failed Latino voters and Texas voters and Democrats in this moment,” said Gonzalez, who previously worked as a top aide to former Vice President Kamala Harris’ campaign. Hinojosa’s race became the ultimate underdog campaign — a push to conquer a state Democrats had all but abandoned, with a candidate from the increasingly conservative Rio Grande Valley who her team was betting could turn out Latino voters in droves. recent_candidates.title: How the GOP Can Win Back Latinos
recent_candidates.author: Juan David Rojas
recent_candidates.excerpt: Politics How the GOP Can Win Back Latinos Voters in South Florida shared their frustrations with The American Conservative . Photo by Saul Martinez/Getty Images It was Election Day in neoconservative South Florida. The torrential rains briefly subsided as I made my way to the local polling station in suburban Fort Lauderdale. A handwritten sign made the following plea to voters: “We didn’t fight terrorists abroad just to come home and watch DEMOCRATS elect them into office.” The state’s younger generations, however, see matters differently. One 20-something Latino I spoke with described himself as a socialist and said that Republicans had nothing to offer young people. Conversely, a young mother of Peruvian heritage told me she typically voted for Republicans but felt Trump needed a wake-up call over broken promises. In the end, Republicans avoided a bloodbath in Florida despite voters—and especially Latinos—swinging hard to the Democrats. The Republican gubernatorial and senatorial candidates Byron Donalds and Ashley Moody narrowly prevailed over Democratic challengers Angie Nixon—who was endorsed by the Democratic Socialists of America (DSA)—and David Jolly. The Miami neocon trio of GOP Reps. Carlos Gimenez, Maria Elvira Salazar, and Mario Diaz-Balart also appear to have survived, though Salazar and Diaz-Balart’s races were still too close to call at the time of writing. recent_candidates.author: Theodore Dalrymple
recent_candidates.excerpt: Culture The destructive urge goes beyond politics and even war. Culture Eating Ourselves Alive The destructive urge goes beyond politics and even war. TakiMag I have only once been asked to be a witness in a libel trial in which the plaintiff denied that he was a cannibal, contrary to the allegation made in print by the defendant, but I suppose that that is infinitely more times than the great majority of people have ever been asked to be such a witness. (I should add that I was to be a witness for the defendant, though my knowledge of the plaintiff’s cannibalism was distinctly limited.) The plaintiff was Charles Taylor, the president of Liberia at the time. He dropped the case against Stephen Ellis, the author of the brilliant and definitive book about the Liberian Civil War. Taylor did so, he said, because of the cost involved, though no one believed this, as he was by then a very rich man. He would have had to testify in London, and in a libel trial all manner of evidence is allowed; it would not have been too difficult to prove that he had no reputation to lose, which is to say, good reputation. What was hardly beyond dispute was that he had used drugged-up children to fight in his guerrilla army in his determination to become president. recent_candidates.title: Watch: Flooding brings Gaza's Civil Defence to declare maximum state of emergency
recent_candidates.author: Mera Aladam
recent_candidates.excerpt: Watch: Flooding brings Gaza's Civil Defence to declare maximum state of emergency Heavy rainfall and strong winds have flooded tens of thousands of displacement tents across Gaza, leaving families exposed to rising floodwaters, freezing conditions and worsening humanitarian needs. Gaza's civil defence declared a maximum state of emergency as overwhelmed rescue teams struggled to respond to thousands of distress calls amid limited resources and inadequate shelter. Rescue teams received over 2000 distress calls since the storm began, while only having capacity to respond to a tenth of the calls received. Heavy rainfall and strong winds have flooded tens of thousands of displacement tents across Gaza, leaving families exposed to rising floodwaters, freezing conditions and worsening humanitarian needs. — Middle East Eye (@MiddleEastEye) November 8, 2026

recent_candidates.title: Rubio says no 'breakthrough' in US-Iran talks
recent_candidates.author: Mera Aladam
recent_candidates.excerpt: Rubio says no 'breakthrough' in US-Iran talks US Secretary of State Marco Rubio suggested that there has been no progress regarding truce talks with Iran, accusing the country of making "unacceptable" demands. "I don’t have any progress to report to you," Rubio told reporters at the Homestead Air Reserve Base in Florida. "You have a number of countries that continue to engage them with different ideas, but I wouldn’t say we’re on the verge of a breakthrough." "The president would always prefer to solve this and every problem diplomatically. Sometimes that’s not possible, unfortunately," he added. Rubio said if there was a chance for a deal, then Washington would "explore it". "Right now, it hasn’t been very productive because the Iranian demands are simply not just unacceptable, but in some cases outrageous and ridiculous and really not realistic," he said. His remarks come ahead of his flight to Paris, where he is set to attend the G7 Foreign Ministers meeting on Monday and Tuesday.

recent_candidates.title: Iranian delegation meet president of Kurdish region in northern Iraq
recent_candidates.author: Fleur Hargreaves
recent_candidates.excerpt: Iranian delegation meet president of Kurdish region in northern Iraq The president of Iraq’s semi-autonomous Kurdistan Regional Government has met with a delegation from Iran on Sunday and reviewed security agreements between Iran and Iraq, including the Kurdish region of northern Iraq, according to a statement from the president's office. Both sides discussed improving security cooperation and mechanisms to help preserve stability in the region, emphasising the “necessity of relying on dialogue, peaceful solutions, and diplomacy to address disputes and challenges”.

recent_candidates.title: Gaza sandbank collapse kills five amid heavy rains
recent_candidates.author: Fleur Hargreaves
recent_candidates.excerpt: Gaza sandbank collapse kills five amid heavy rains At least five people have been killed, including three children, after heavy rains caused a sandbank to collapse in central Gaza's Deir al-Balah, Wafa news reported on Sunday. A civil defence spokesman added that five wounded people had been pulled out of the rubble after their tents were hit, and teams are continuing to search for survivors. The incident comes amid worsening conditions faced by displaced Palestinians in Gaza, as national and internation institutions warned heavy rainfall and bad weather require urgent intervention and the provision of safe shelter and winter supplies.

recent_candidates.title: Iraq has agreed with the US to allow oil exports through Hormuz, minister says
recent_candidates.author: Fleur Hargreaves
recent_candidates.excerpt: Iraq has agreed with the US to allow oil exports through Hormuz, minister says Iraq has reached understandings with the US to allow Iraqi oil exports through the Strait of Hormuz via a shipping lane near Oman, Foreign Minister Fuad Hussein said in an interview with Al Jazeera. He added that Iraq's losses from the Iran war and disruptions to oil exports had reached $60 billion. Hussein also told Al Jazeera that the US Treasury has asked Iraq to close all border crossings with Iran except for two as part of Washington's policy of increasing economic pressure on Tehran, with one of the exceptions being in the Kurdistan region.

recent_candidates.title: Why nobody stopped Russell Brand
recent_candidates.author: Poppy Sowerby
recent_candidates.excerpt: It’s always the ones you most expect. That, at least, has been the conclusion online after the rape conviction of Russell Brand. Rather than admit that Brand’s conspicuous, hypersexual persona was a rather effective sleight of hand — one which successfully distracted production companies and audiences from his criminal private life for two decades — social media has spent the past week telling itself it can spot a wrong’un a mile off. So it is that long-buried clips of Brand making rape jokes on Channel 4 quiz shows have popped up on our timelines: see , these posts say, this is what a rapist looks like . It’s a reaction I can understand. Watching back clips of Brand’s big-haired heyday, it is difficult to understand why nobody raised the alarm. There’s the recording of Brand offering to send his personal assistant to Jimmy Savile, naked; “Nothing wrong with that,” warbles the elder predator. There’s the clip of him on a talk show, bragging about convincing women to “trust me” by posing as gay — before “bang! Pregnant” . There’s the one where he jokes about dragging a woman “into a cubicle” to “show her my pubicles” (a similar account cropped up in court). This was a man whose recurring gag was being vulgar, boastful, libidinous and frightening. In isolation, these snippets are shocking — but lest we forget, these qualities were once the very foundations of late-night television. recent_candidates.title: Why my sister is marrying a dying man
recent_candidates.author: Matthew Gasda
recent_candidates.excerpt: In a week, barring setbacks, my sister will marry a man dying of cancer, in a small church in Akron, Ohio. Elizabeth met George in person six months ago for the first time, after a courtship of six months of talking on the phone (she lives in Pennsylvania; they met online). Their first date ended up in the hospital after my sister noticed that George’s skin was jaundiced; tests revealed that he had pancreatic cancer, which has since become metastatic. The new couple was able to spend the summer together, in relatively good spirits, road-tripping to different clinics to get second, third, and fourth opinions on George’s tumor, but George’s prognosis has not improved; they have not found a treatment that will meaningfully push back the horizon of death. They will get married with the unendurable awareness that they have only a few weeks or a few months together. Elizabeth says that she was in denial this summer and so was George. They could let themselves think that pancreatic cancer was misdiagnosed as pancreatitis. They talked about having five kids together. They had a life in mind. They’ll be lucky to have five weeks, let alone five months. I wanted to write about them, with their permission, because I think their kind of story is the most important in the world. The tendency of modern society is to remove death and suffering, leaving us unaware of the real stakes of living. D’autre part, il s’agit de cultiver l’imaginaire d’une province préservée et contemplative, incarné par des lieux comme Dali, Lijiang ou Shangri-La. recent_candidates.title: Economía rusa: las elevadas pérdidas en Ucrania lastran el presupuesto del Estado y de las regiones
recent_candidates.author: Ramona Bloj
recent_candidates.excerpt: El viernes 30 de octubre, el gobernador de la región de Belgorod, Alexander Shuvaev, anunció que la indemnización que la región abona a las familias de los soldados fallecidos en el frente de Ucrania se reduciría a un tercio. Esta indemnización ha pasado de 3 millones de rublos a un millón, es decir, unos 11.000 euros, frente a los aproximadamente 33.000 que se pagaban anteriormente. Desde principios de año, al menos diez regiones han reducido, aplazado o suprimido esta prestación. Según el economista Janis Kluge, estas reducciones son notables , sobre todo teniendo en cuenta que el importe de las indemnizaciones se había mantenido estable desde el inicio de la invasión, en febrero de 2022. El fenómeno se está acelerando en un contexto de deterioro de las finanzas regionales: 71 de las 83 regiones rusas registraron un déficit presupuestario el año pasado, según los datos recopilados por la agencia de calificación Expert RA. Las diez regiones que han reducido, aplazado o suprimido las indemnizaciones registran un déficit medio de casi el 10% de sus ingresos en 2025, frente al 6% de las demás. A finales de septiembre, el Gobierno presentó ante la Duma Estatal, la cámara baja del Parlamento ruso, un proyecto de ley que prevé conceder a las autoridades un plazo mucho más amplio para abonar las indemnizaciones debidas a las familias de los combatientes fallecidos. recent_candidates.author: Adrián Ortega
recent_candidates.excerpt: Los Cincinnati Bengals se hicieron este domingo con el triunfo ante los Atlanta Falcons, a los que batieron con claridad por 17-34 en el segundo partido de la NFL, la liga estadounidense de fútbol americano, en Madrid y después de imponer su actual momento y estilo, comandado por el trabajo de la dupla Joe Burrow-Ja’Marr Chase. 78.660 espectadores, 50 más que el año pasado, se dieron cita en el Estadio Santiago Bernabéu para presenciar la segunda parada de la historia en España de la NFL, mucho más vistosa, como se auguraba, y pese a un segundo acto algo menos brillante, que la del año pasado con los Miami Dolphins y los Washington Commanders , aunque sin tanta emoción porque los Bengals no dieron demasiadas opciones a su rival. Cincinnati venía a Madrid en mejor forma y lo demostró para encadenar su cuarta victoria consecutiva y alcanzar a los Pittsburgh Steelers en el liderato de la División Norte de la Conferencia Americana con un balance de 6-2 para mantener su candidatura a la Super Bowl en su mejor arranque desde el año 2015. recent_candidates.title: Bezzecchi gana y Marc Márquez se queda a las puertas del título
recent_candidates.author: THE OBJECTIVE
recent_candidates.excerpt: El piloto español Marc Márquez (Ducati) ha dado un paso más hacia el título de MotoGP al finalizar segundo en la carrera de este domingo en el Gran Premio de Catar , decimonovena cita del Mundial de motociclismo, en la que se ha impuesto el italiano Marco Bezzecchi (Aprilia) y Raúl Fernández (Aprilia) ha terminado tercero, mientras que Jorge Martín (Aprilia), rival del de Cervera por el campeonato, ha concluido séptimo. Márquez, ganador de la esprint, defendió su segundo puesto de salida y sumó 20 valiosos puntos que le permitirán llegar a Portugal, dentro de dos fines de semana, con 60 puntos de ventaja sobre Martín y 74 sobre Bezzecchi. Si gana la carrera corta en Portimao, será campeón hagan lo que hagan sus adversarios. En su primer ‘match point’ por el título, Márquez cayó de la segunda a la tercera posición una vez apagados los semáforos en Lusail, con Bezzecchi defendiendo su posición de privilegio por delante de Raúl Fernández. Por detrás, Martín conseguía pasar de la undécima a la octava plaza en la primera vuelta. Marc Márquez se lleva la victoria en Malasia y tendrá en Catar su primera opción de título THE OBJECTIVE Mientras el italiano comenzaba a dejar atrás al de la Aprilia satélite, los dos contendientes por el campeonato cedieron una plaza poco después, aunque consiguieron recuperarla para asentarse de nuevo en la tercera y la octava, respectivamente, a partir del sexto giro, cuando el de Cervera le devolvió la pasada a Pedro Acosta (KTM). recent_candidates.title: Aterriza en Barcelona de urgencia un avión con un bebé que requería asistencia médica
recent_candidates.author: THE OBJECTIVE
recent_candidates.excerpt: Un avión en el que viajaba un bebé de pocos meses y que necesitaba asistencia médica rápidamente ha aterrizado de urgencia este domingo en el aeropuerto de Barcelona , donde se ha activado el protocolo para la evacuación en ambulancia del menor. Los controladores aéreos han informado de que la tripulación de un vuelo que cubría la ruta entre Casablanca y Estambul ha pedido desviarse de urgencia al aeropuerto de Barcelona ya que llevaban a bordo a un bebé de apenas unos meses con problemas médicos que requerían atención urgente. Los coordinadores han priorizado entonces el aterrizaje de la nave con una aproximación directa a la pista 24L , la más cercana al mar y la empleada habitualmente para los despegues. Como consecuencia de ello, ha sido necesario parar momentáneamente los despegues y hacer esperar el resto de aterrizajes. Un avión privado con nueve personas a bordo se estrella en una zona residencial de Florida THE OBJECTIVE Cuando la nave ha tomado tierra, el avión ha quedado estacionado en un espacio muy próximo a la salida de pista, donde los servicios médicos han podido actuar de inmediato y realizar la evacuación. Los controladores, que han expresado su deseo de que el pequeño se recupere pronto y bien, han agradecido en las redes el trabajo hecho en este caso por todos los servicios implicados, como el del personal sanitario y las tripulaciones.
